body:
Model context, overall session context and session compression settings make huge difference.  Point your agent at the docs, tell it about your work flow, and have it recommend some changes.  For example, I run Qwen3.6 MOE on my M1 Max Studio, so I run a ctx of 256k, but the type of model it is (deltanet hybrid) is bandwidth bound, not memory, so I can run compress when I reach 90% instead of the default 50%, and take it down to 20%.  I still mean to play with it more, but its been working fine for my setup.  

Different models have different requirements (a cloud model with a 1M ctx is a different thing and will just have regular context rot around 250k and up, but mine work fine at 500k as long as I keep to current stuff it has attention and not old stuff, and I also do a lot of /steer during an inference; not a lot of new cycles)

There is A LOT of stuff that goes into a session, skills list, all the file system reads, web pages, every single character, json brace is a potential token, so managing your context is important overall.  I spent a couple months learning about it, and my workflows to get a good baseline understanding.  

I have lots of other things I have learned over time as well.  But you must remember that physics and autoregressive AI realities are HARD limits, you can only work with them, against them you fail (like Yoda told Luke... lmao)
